column1: # One program's rows of the -db fixtures (see README.md here for the columns and the loader in ../db_search_fixtures.py).
# Rows db.sa.*.5 (OF4a): -outfmt 5 (BLAST XML) of BLASTN and BLASTP, each the search of the db.sa.*.8 row of the same stem (stdout is the XML document; hit ids gnl|BL_ORD_ID|N).

# Rows db.sa.{blastx,tblastn,tblastx}.*.5 and db.x5.* (OF4b): the same for BLASTX, TBLASTN and TBLASTX; db.x5.* use the mixed query files tests/fasta/outfmt0/x5_* (each with a query without hits), db.x5.*.nohit_all has no hit for any query.

# Rows db.sa.*.1[56], db.x16.* and db.x16_*taxid.* (OF5a for BLASTP and BLASTN, OF5b for BLASTX, TBLASTN and TBLASTX): -outfmt 16 (BLAST XML2) and 15 (BLAST JSON) of all five programs, the search of the .5 or .8 row of the same stem where the covers cell says so; BLASTDB=DIR, BATCH_SIZE=N, ARCHIVE_FORMAT=X and PRE_FETCH_SEQS_LIMIT=N tokens in extra_args are environment variables of the NCBI run and of LOSAT's.

# Rows db.sa.* (line OF, OF3b): -outfmt 8 (Seq-annot, ASN.1 text) and 12 (Seq-annot, JSON) and, in the ids ending .9 (OF3c), 9 (Seq-annot, binary ASN.1; the fixture files are binary, see fixtures/db_search/.gitattributes); freeze them alone with `freeze --only db.sa.`.

# Rows db.x16.blastx.mix.13, db.sa.x16_ttaxid.good.13, db.sa.x16_xtaxid.good.14 (OF5c part 2, BLASTX, TBLASTN and TBLASTX): the same for the programs of part 2, the search of the .16 row of the same stem.

# Rows db.sa.*.1[34] (OF5c, BLASTP and BLASTN): -outfmt 14 and 13 (side files and a master file) of the search of the .16/.15 row of the same stem. The files column is xinclude: the runner adds `-out <tmp>/<row_id>.out`; the master is frozen as <row_id>.out (stdout_sha256, stdout_bytes; standard output is empty), the side files as <row_id>.out_<n>.xml|json (side_sha256, in order). A row of the old form has 12 cells and no files columns (LOSAT/tests/xinclude_fixtures.py).

# Rows db.numdesc.* (line NP, O1b): -num_descriptions and -num_alignments (blast_args.cpp:2894-2973); the last one is NCBI's error for a hit list size of 0 (rc 1, empty stdout); freeze them alone with `freeze --only db.numdesc.`.
# Rows db.blastp.culling_* and db.tblastn.culling_* (line NP, O3b): -culling_limit with -db; freeze them alone with `freeze --only db.blastp.culling_` / `--only db.tblastn.culling_`.

# Rows db.sa.arch.tbn.* (line OF, OF8b2): -outfmt 11 (BLAST archive, ASN.1 text; ARCHIVE_FORMAT=bin|BIN: binary; =foo: nothing) of TBLASTN with `-db tests/db_search/arch_tbn_snucl` (version 4, no -parse_seqids: makeblastdb -in tests/fasta/outfmt11/arch_tbn_s.fna -dbtype nucl -title snucdb -blastdb_version 4; .nhr .nin .nsq kept), each with the .8 and .5 rows of the same search so that check_archive_layout.py predict rebuilds the archive; freeze them alone with `freeze --only db.sa.arch.tbn.`.

# Rows db.id.* (line DBID, ID2a): BLASTP and BLASTX against the databases with parsed Seq-ids tests/db_search/ids/prot_v5 and prot_v4 (make_ids.py: every Seq-id form, several definition lines, GIs, titles NCBI makes from the Seq-ids), every format they write (version 4: outfmt 0, 5, 6); the queries tests/db_search/ids/ids_q.faa and ids_q.fna (the second hits weakly, the third not at all). With BLASTDB=tests/seqdb/taxdb/good the XML2 and JSON descriptions name each taxid (db.id.*.taxdb*; refuse_v5 holds a taxid that taxonomy database does not know between two it knows). Rows db.id.psiblast.* (DBID psiblast): psiblast's first round against the same databases (outfmt 0, the tabular id fields, version 4, outfmt 7 with a taxonomy database) and two of the rejections, which name PSIBLAST. Rejection rows: subjects whose Seq-align ids match (NCBI joins their hits in outfmt 0, 5 and 13 to 16; tests/db_search/ids/pfound_v5 since line DBID N1), sequences NCBI's formatters do not find by their Seq-align id (bbs|, gnl|PIG|, nat| and every other sequence of tests/seqid/db/variants, which has no ISAM; query ids_qw.faa; lcl|777 before gi|777), a title NCBI makes from the taxonomy database, the records of tests/db_search/ids/refuse_v5 (make_ids.py: titles whose end NCBI rewrites from the taxids, an outfmt 0 description id over 65 bytes and a title of punctuation, both of which NCBI's outfmt 0 does not end on; each query hits its own record alone with -evalue 1e-20). BLASTX makes these refusals of a batch's reported sequences after the first lines of outfmt 0, as its other refusals of reported sequences; it holds outfmt 5 and 13 to 16 of a database with parsed Seq-ids, so those documents are dropped.

# Rows db.id.{blastn,tblastn,tblastx}.* (line DBID, ID2b): BLASTN (megablast; -task blastn and dc-megablast in db.id.blastn.{blastn,dc}.*), TBLASTN and TBLASTX against the nucleotide databases with parsed Seq-ids tests/db_search/ids/nucl_v5 and nucl_v4 (make_ids.py: the Seq-id forms of tests/seqid/fasta/nucl_ids.fa with the GenBank, EMBL and DDBJ accessions each under prefixes of its own partner, several definition lines, GIs, titles NCBI makes from the Seq-ids), every format they write (version 4: outfmt 0, 5, 6); queries tests/seqid/fasta/qnucl.fa and qprot.fa (the second has no hit); TBLASTN and TBLASTX with -max_hsps 1. Rejection rows: lcl|777 before gi|777 (nrefuse_v5; NCBI's formatters do not find the sequence by gi|777), gb|AF000040.1| and gb|AF000040| in the two volumes of the alias njoined (NCBI joins their hits in outfmt 0, 5 and 13 to 16), a title NCBI makes from the taxonomy database (BLASTN and TBLASTX make these refusals after the first lines of outfmt 0, as their other refusals of reported sequences).

# Rows db.id.*.found.* (line DBID N1): Seq-align ids by which NCBI's formatters find another sequence of the database first (tests/db_search/ids/pfound_v5, pfound_v4, nfound_v5, nfound_v4; make_ids.py): NCBI writes that sequence's names and counts the identities against its letters, or stops; LOSAT refuses such a sequence in the formats that read its Bioseq (outfmt 0, 5, 6, 7, 10, 13 to 17), unless the other sequence holds the same definition lines and letters (pdup_ab, an alias of two copies of one record), and writes the Seq-annots as NCBI. The ncbi rows: outfmt 8, a -negative_seqidlist that leaves the other sequence out, the orders in which each id finds its own sequence, the alias of two copies. The protein joined rows db.id.{blastp,blastx}.joined.* search pfound_v5 (pairs 4 and 5).

# Rows db.id.*.found.taxid.* (line DBID N1b): the same record with other taxids in the two databases of an alias (tests/db_search/ids/pdup_at, pdup_tu, pdup_no, pdupe_at, ndup_at; make_ids.py --copytaxid-only, make_found_fasta.py): NCBI shows for both the copy that its lookup gives first, with that copy's taxids; LOSAT writes the rows where no report writes taxids or their names and refuses the sequence in outfmt 13 to 16 and the tabular staxid, staxids and name fields, and in every format where a title can depend on the taxids or the taxonomy database's texts depend on the copy NCBI fetches (texts of opening where only one copy has a taxid, the offset error of a taxid a copy holds, which each volume writes once)

# Rows db.id.join.* (line DBID N3): copies of one record that follow each other in a hit list (tests/db_search/ids/pjoin_abc, pjoin_abt, njoin_abc, njoin_abt and the list "pjoin_a pjoin_b pjoin_c"; make_ids.py --join-only, make_join_fasta.py: r1 in a, b and c, r3 with two definition lines and two HSPs in a and b, r6 the letters of r1 under another id, which comes between the copy in c and those in b and a): NCBI's outfmt 0, 5 and 13 to 16 show the alignments of following copies in one hit (one description line and heading, Hsp_num going on), -num_descriptions, -num_alignments and psiblast's cut to -max_target_seqs count them as one subject; the tabular formats keep a row per copy (their qcovs and qcovus count the group). LOSAT joins copies of one record (the same definition lines but for their taxids) and still refuses other sequences whose Seq-align ids match (db.id.*.joined.*, also with qcovs or qcovus), and copies with other letters (pjoin_ax, njoin_ax); njoin_tab holds two copies with taxid 9606 for the heading under a taxid list

# Rows db.id.title.* (line DBID N1b L1): copies with other taxids whose title NCBI can make from the taxids (tests/db_search/ids/pdupe_at, ndupe_at without a title, psubj_at with lcl|Subject_1 without a title, psubjb_at with lcl|Subject_2 and a title ending in ]; make_ids.py --titlesrc-only, make_found_fasta.py) and one sequence lcl|Subject_1 (nsubj_t) or lcl|Subject_3 beside gb|EEN00007.1| (nsubjg_t) without a title with a taxid: NCBI generates the title of the Bioseq it fetches, from its source where the taxonomy database names the taxid (BLASTDB=tests/seqdb/taxdb/good; no_btd names none), only for outfmt 0 and the tabular word that replaces a lcl|Subject_ id; LOSAT refuses the copies there (and in the formats of taxids) and writes the other formats, and refuses a nucleotide word made from the source where a printed id shows it

# Rows db.id.bare.* (line DBID H3): one sequence of a database without parsed Seq-ids with an empty title and taxid 9606 (tests/db_search/ids/nbare_t, pbare_t; make_ids.py --emptytitle-only, make_found_fasta.py): its Bioseq has a source for the taxid as one with parsed Seq-ids has, so NCBI's outfmt 0 makes the title from it where the taxonomy database names the taxid (Homo sapiens; unnamed protein product [Homo sapiens]); LOSAT refuses that outfmt 0 and writes the other formats, and the outfmt 0 of a taxonomy database that names nothing (no_btd) or of none

# Rows db.id.*.ord.* (line DBID N2a): sequences whose only Seq-id is gnl|BL_ORD_ID|n (tests/db_search/ids/pord_v5, pord_v4, nord_v5, nord_v4 and the alias pord_vx of pord_v5 and pord_x; make_ids.py, make_ord_fasta.py). With n the sequence's number in its volume it is read as a sequence without parsed Seq-ids, which NCBI finds; another n is a Seq-id that makeblastdb -parse_seqids stored as written, by which NCBI's formatters find no sequence (Unknown, or a stop in the tabular formats) or, through an alias, another one: LOSAT refuses it in the formats that read its Bioseq and writes n plus the first ordinal id of the volume in the Seq-annots, as NCBI. A first header with such an id gives the database parsed Seq-ids (nord_v5).

# Rows db.id.*.look.* (line DBID N2b): Seq-align ids that LOSAT refused by their kind before N2b and that NCBI's formatters look up like any other (tests/db_search/ids/plook_v5, plook_v4, nlook_v5, nlook_v4 and the alias plook_vz of plook_v5 and plook_z; make_ids.py, make_look_fasta.py): version 5 finds bbs|, nat| and lcl|<integer> by their LMDB keys unless an earlier sequence holds the key, version 4 finds neither bbs| nor nat|, no version finds gnl|PIG|, and gnl|BL_ORD_ID|n of the sequence's own number is found also beside another id. LOSAT refuses where the lookup gives no sequence or another one first, or where another sequence holds the Seq-align id, also in another letter case (tests/db_search/ids/pshare_v5, pshare_v4, the aliases pshare_ab and pshare_cd, nshare_v5, pdup_abc: NCBI's scope can show that sequence where both are reported), in the formats that read the Bioseq.

# Rows db.id.*.weak.* (line DBID N2c): Seq-ids that NCBI's scope matches weakly (CSeq_id_Textseq_Tree::FindMatch: an accession without a version finds the same accession with one, an id of accession and name finds the name-only id, a name-only id finds an id of that name and an accession, a pir or prf accession-only id finds the name-only id with that text as name; not the other way) in databases with parsed Seq-ids (tests/db_search/ids/pweak_v5, pweak_v4, nweak_v5, nweak_v4; make_ids.py, make_weak_fasta.py). LOSAT refuses a query read with -parse_deflines whose id a reported sequence's Seq-align id matches weakly (NCBI shows the query for the subject; .q.* rows) and, with PRE_FETCH_SEQS_LIMIT=N set to anything but 2147483647 (a PRE_FETCH_SEQS_LIMIT=N token in extra_args is an environment variable of both programs; NCBI reads the reported sequences one by one when N is 0 or below the batch's Seq-align count; LOSAT counts each batch since line DBID weakbatch, rows db.id.wkb.*), a reported sequence whose Seq-align id can match weakly an id of another sequence (NCBI writes that sequence's names for it; .pf.* rows; in a version 5 database NCBI's lookup is not reproduced, so any Seq-align id with a name and any pir or prf id is refused without it, in version 4 the lookup decides) and, in the rows .r.* (pweak_r_v5, pweak_r_v4; review 1), a name in another letter case, a prf holder, a pir accession found by a prf name and by an emb accession with a version, each a pair S, T with T's first definition line holding the second id (NCBI writes T's names for S). The ncbi rows: the direction NCBI does not match, the same searches without the variable or at 2147483647, outfmt 8, and (version 4 only) the sequences with no weak holder.

# Rows db.id.tf.* (line DBID tabfields): tabular field lists that read nothing of a reported sequence with parsed Seq-ids (no subject id, title, taxonomy, strand, slen or field of the alignment's letters; report::tabular::reads_subject) on the databases of the rows above whose subjects NCBI's formatters find as another sequence or not at all: NCBI writes the same rows whatever its lookup finds, and so does LOSAT; the .reject rows are what still refuses: a list that reads the sequence (sseqid, slen, nident, sframe in BLASTX), and what the batches' prefetch reads for such a list (another sequence whose definition lines do not hold the Seq-align id: NCBI stops; TBLASTX's minus-strand Seq-align of a sequence the prefetch gets no Bioseq of: NCBI warns).

# Rows db.id.pfw.* (line DBID pfwarn): NCBI's `Error pre-fetching sequence data` where a batch's prefetch fails at a subject that no report reads (a Seq-align id whose lookup fails, a minus-strand Seq-align of a subject without a Bioseq; BLASTN -ungapped takes the strand of a subject's first HSP), after the texts of the loads (BLASTDB=tests/seqdb/taxdb/<variant>), on the taxid copies tests/db_search/ids/ntag_t5, nlook_t4, pshare_t5 (make_ids.py --pfwarn-only) and nlook_v4, pshare_v5; the two losat-rejection rows are a failed lookup in a batch whose other subjects' loads write a text.

# Rows db.id.wkb.* (line DBID weakbatch): the weak matches of NCBI's scope (rows db.id.*.weak.*) with a positive PRE_FETCH_SEQS_LIMIT, which NCBI counts against each query batch's Seq-aligns: a batch at or below the limit prefetches, loading each sequence by its own id (the ncbi rows: every program, both database versions, outfmt 0 and 5, a batch of BATCH_SIZE=1 beside one above the limit), a batch above it reads its sequences one by one and can show the other sequence (the rejection rows); psiblast's rounds (db.id.wkb.ps.*: a round that makes the next PSSM reads the sequences before the cut, and NCBI's PSSM puts following hits whose Seq-align ids Match in one row). The queries ids/wkb_q8x2.faa and ids/wkb_n1x2.fna are pweak_q8.faa and nweak_q1.fna twice (joined by 30 X, 40 N: two HSPs a subject), ids/wkb_q0_q4x3.faa is pweak_q0.faa then pweak_q4.faa three times.

# Rows db.tm.* (line DBID, item T): NCBI's messages about the taxonomy database (BLASTDB=tests/seqdb/taxdb/<variant>) in the formats that prefetch the reported subjects (outfmt 0, 5, 6, 7, 17), all five programs: the open messages (bad_magic, count_larger), the volume lookup of a taxid at the last index entry (offset_last_past_end, databases x16_*taxid_99990), several batches (BATCH_SIZE=100), a batch whose first queries have warnings of their own (x16_*qinv: letters that give no Karlin-Altschul parameters, a query without letters), a database with parsed Seq-ids, and a taxonomy database without messages (good). Review 1 (db.tm.bp.fast.*, db.tm.bp.2vol.*, db.tm.*.cache*): blastp-fast with two query blocks (tests/db_search/tm_fast_q289.faa), an alias of two volumes (tests/db_search/tm_2vol), and the volumes tm_cache150 (refused: a taxid of the slot of the offset error's taxid in NCBI's per-volume taxonomy cache) and tm_cache151 (its control); tests/db_search/README.md says how they were made. Item P1 (db.tm.psi.*, db.tm.bp.off0.*): psiblast's prefetch of its traceback hit lists (tests/db_search/tm_psi: a subject beyond -max_target_seqs 1), one query per batch, and PRE_FETCH_SEQS_LIMIT turning the prefetch off (0, or below the batch's Seq-aligns: lim6 against lim7; fields that read no subject: qe), blastp too; review 1: subjects beyond the cut whose Seq-align id is found nowhere (tm_psi_pig), fails (tm_psi_rz) or is held by another sequence (tm_psi_held: no taxid, no lookup; tm_psi_held2: taxid 99990, refused). Item P2 (db.tm.{bn,tn,bx,tx}.off0.*, db.tm.tn.lim*, db.tm.tx.lim1.*, db.tm.{bn,bx}.ug.*): PRE_FETCH_SEQS_LIMIT turning the prefetch off in BLASTN, TBLASTN, BLASTX and TBLASTX: the messages after the warnings of the query whose report fetches (x16_*qinv), none for fields that read no subject (qe; BLASTN's formatter also for nident), outfmt 5 (warnings in the Iteration messages), the volume lookup once per volume and taxid (lastoff), and the batch's Seq-aligns at the limit: one per HSP of a gapped search (tblastn lim2 against lim3), one per subject of an ungapped one (tblastx lim1, blastn and blastx -ungapped lim2); review 1: the subject's frame with a coordinate field in the translated programs (frame, sframe), and a run whose batches never prefetch and whose fields read no subject on tm_cache150 (not refused).

# Rows db.im.* (line DBID P3): PRE_FETCH_SEQS_LIMIT=2147483647, at which NCBI's s_PreFetchSeqs prefetches before it tests the format (blast_app_util.cpp:738-740), so also for the Seq-annots outfmt 8, 9 and 12 (not the archive, written without the prefetch): the taxonomy database's messages of db.tm.* after the reader's messages (BLASTN, TBLASTN, BLASTX, TBLASTX, BLASTP), the variable unset as a control, and the subjects with parsed Seq-ids that the prefetch reads by their Seq-align ids: lcl|777 before gi|777 without and with a Seq-align whose length the prefetch asks for; losat-rejection: a lookup that fails, another sequence whose definition lines do not hold the id (NCBI exit 2; also psiblast's list beyond -max_target_seqs, which NCBI prefetches at any value) and copies whose texts depend on the copy NCBI reads (as in outfmt 6).

# Rows db.tfast.* (line DI4, dropin-survey-20261029): TBLASTN -task tblastn-fast and -word_size 6 and 7 with -db (the database tests/db_search/tfast_amr of synthetic contigs with AMR genes, and tslice), AMRFinderPlus's two tblastn calls; freeze them alone with `freeze --only db.tfast.`.

# Rows db.sc1.* (line NP, series SC, SC1): TBLASTN -matrix, -gapopen and -gapextend with -db (tests/db_search/tslice) in composition modes 0 and 2, IDENTITY's reset to mode 0 with its warnings; freeze them alone with `freeze --only db.sc1.`.

# Rows db.sc11.* (line NP, series SC, SC11): TBLASTN's compressed lookup table (-task tblastn-fast, -word_size 6 and 7) with the matrices other than BLOSUM62 with -db, the epilog's threshold and window; freeze them alone with `freeze --only db.sc11.`.

# Rows db.tab.tbn.* and db.tab.tbx.* (line CLI, C2b): TBLASTN and TBLASTX custom tabular reports (-outfmt "6|7|10|20 [delim=X] <fields>") with -db: every identifier, alignment and taxonomy field on databases with and without -parse_seqids and with taxids (tslice / xslice, ids/nucl_v4, ids/nucl_v5, x16_ntaxid), the taxdb cases (staxids with a taxdb: ncbi; sscinames with a taxdb: losat-rejection), delim= forms, NCBI's delimiter error (delim=/ with frames, rc 1), frames without a counts field, -query_loc, TBLASTN -db_gencode 4 / -matrix BLOSUM45 -word_size 2 -comp_based_stats 0, TBLASTX -query_gencode 4 -db_gencode 11, and the drop-in calls of CORPUS (T03, UNI02, MOB07, KLB03 for TBLASTN; TX03, GAL18 for TBLASTX); the -subject rows are tab.tbn.* and tab.tbx.* in outfmt0_manifest.tsv. Freeze them alone with `freeze --only db.tab.tbn.` / `freeze --only db.tab.tbx.`.

# Rows db.tf.* (DI-8a, dropin-survey-20261029/DI8): -taxids, -taxidlist, -negative_taxids, -negative_taxidlist and -no_taxid_expansion with -db on the version 5 databases of tests/db_search/taxfilter (tfp protein, tfn nucleotide in two volumes; make_taxfilter.py), the taxonomy file taxfilter/taxonomy4blast.sqlite3 by the BLASTDB=DIR token; db.tf.*.empty.6 are LOSAT refusals of a list that excludes every OID (NCBI searches an empty database).

# Rows db.gis.* (dropin DI-7): -show_gis on databases with parsed Seq-ids (ids/prot_v5, prot_v4, nucl_v5, nucl_v4: every Seq-id form, GIs, several definition lines): outfmt 0 shows gi|N| and the FASTA form of the id; outfmt 5 and 6, and a database without parsed Seq-ids, do not change.

# Rows db.sl.* (DI-8b, dropin-survey-20261029/DI8): -seqidlist and -negative_seqidlist with -db on the version 5 databases tests/db_search/taxfilter/tfp and tfn (two volumes) and tests/db_search/ids/prot_v5 and nucl_v5 (every Seq-id form), the version 4 databases ids/prot_v4 and nucl_v4 (string ISAM), with the lists of tests/db_search/seqidlist (make_seqidlist.py: text lists in NCBI's token forms, binary lists in blastdb_aliastool's format); the negative lists on ids/prot_v5, prot_v4, nucl_v5 and nucl_v4 (db.sl.bp.nforms.6, bp.v4neg.6, bp.v4gi.6, bn.nforms.6, bn.v4neg.6) are LOSAT refusals too: those databases hold sequences whose every definition line has only a gi or a ti, which a negative seqid list leaves without a line (NCBI drops their hits without notice, DI-8b DECISIONS 17); freeze them alone with `freeze --only db.sl.`.

# Rows db.sp.* (dropin DI-7): -searchsp with -db (the five programs): the effective search space of the E-values, the cutoffs, `Effective search space used:`, Statistics_eff-space and the archive; -dbsize stays in the length adjustment; NCBI sets OLD_FSC at any -searchsp value (blast_args.cpp:303-307), so the protein programs lose the Gumbel block.

# Rows db.oldfsc.* (line SW, env parity G1): the environment variable OLD_FSC (any value, the empty one too), with which NCBI's protein programs have no Gumbel block (blast_stat.c:921-923): the E-values and cutoffs without the finite-size correction, as with `-searchsp 0` (NCBI sets OLD_FSC for any -searchsp, blast_args.cpp:303-307) but with the archive's options of a search without -searchsp; -ungapped frees the block anyway (blast_setup.c:521-527; BLASTX, the program of these three that LOSAT searches ungapped). BLASTP, BLASTX, TBLASTN, PSIBLAST (PS5c) and RPSBLAST (PS11c-2, rows db.rps.mini.oldfsc.* in rpsblast.tsv) read it (`old_fsc`).

# Rows db.acbs.* (line SW, env parity G2+G3): the environment variable ADAPTIVE_CBS (any value, the empty one too), with which NCBI's protein programs keep a larger preliminary hit list with composition-based statistics (blast_hits.c:43-70) and, for a hit list size below 1000, cut it by E-value when the stream closes (BlastHSPCBSStreamClose, blast_hspstream.c:816-864; not PSIBLAST, whose traceback size is the preliminary size): tests/db_search/acbs and acbs_n (README.md there), the 1,050 vs 1,500 lists of 700 composition-biased and 1,000 ordinary subjects; rows wrap/rej: -max_target_seqs whose preliminary size wraps in NCBI's int (BLASTX).

# Rows db.pd.* (dropin DI-7): -parse_deflines with -db (the five programs): the query ids of Query=, qseqid, qacc, qaccver, qgi, the XML query id and title, the Seq-aligns and the archive (Bioseq ids, seq-loc-list when no id is local); query files of tests/db_search/make_pd.py; losat-rejection rows are LOSAT's refusals of what NCBI's scope shows as another sequence (dropin-survey-20261029/DI7/DECISIONS.md 7, 8).

# Rows db.ec.* (DI-8c, dropin-survey-20261029/DI8): a taxid or seqid list that keeps no sequence of the database (tests/db_search/taxfilter/tfp, tfn; ids/prot_v4, nucl_v4): NCBI searches nothing, warns `Filtering resulted in an empty database.` for each query of a searched batch and reports its statistics from the length of OID 0 and one sequence; query files of tests/db_search/seqidlist (make_seqidlist.py); freeze them alone with `freeze --only db.ec.`.

# Rows db.sa8.* (DI-8d, dropin-survey-20261029/DI8): a positive taxid or seqid list writes the `ext` `use_this_seqid` on each Seq-align (outfmt 8, 9, 11, 12; tests/db_search/taxfilter/tfp, tfn; useseqid/ for the id forms), limits the outfmt 0 heading to the lines it names; a negative list writes none; freeze them alone with `freeze --only db.sa8.`.

# Rows db.mdb.* (DI-8f, dropin-survey-20261029/DI8): -db with several names (`-db "a b"`: one virtual database, as NCBI's CSeqDB) on the databases of tests/db_search/multidb (make_multidb.py): version 5 pairs with taxids (pa pb, na nb; nb and pb hold a copy of a sequence of the other), a version 5 database without -parse_seqids (nnp), version 4 pairs (n4a n4b, p4a p4b), one base name in two directories (d1/g d2/g), an empty title (et), an alias (al), a seqid list (sl.txt); the names given twice, in the other order, in double quotes (Galaxy) and with extra spaces; db.mdb.bn.v4v5.6 is NCBI's exit 2 for both versions; db.mdb.bn.mixed.6 and db.mdb.bn.aliasdup.0 are LOSAT refusals.
